llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed context and memory pipeline that modifies workspace context files for its stated purpose, with no evidence of hidden exfiltration, credential use, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The file reads, memory retrieval, Context Pack generation, AGENTS.md update, validation scripts, and optional memory commit workflow all align with the stated purpose of standardizing agent memory/context handling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad natural-language triggers and substring routing, which can cause over-routing or accidental persistence, but these behaviors are visible in the artifacts and tied to the context-pipeline purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation copies bundled files into context_pipeline, asks the agent to patch AGENTS.md, and runs local validation/watchdog scripts; this is disclosed and does not show hidden network activity beyond the explicit clawhub install command.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local memory files such as memory/always_on.md, topic files, now/open-loops, and MEMORY.md; this is sensitive but proportionate for a memory retrieval pipeline and scoped to documented memory paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The apply flow changes AGENTS.md and context_pipeline, debug/audit modes may write .openclaw/context-runs artifacts, and the memory commit workflow writes durable memory files; users should treat these as persistent behavior changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want an agent to use local memory files as routine context and to make persistent workspace changes when asked to apply or memorize. Review the AGENTS.md diff and any memory-file changes, and use debug/audit modes only when you are comfortable writing run artifacts to disk.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill does not include a separate permissions manifest, but the artifact text clearly discloses workspace file reads/writes and the scripts are limited to copying, validating, or checking documented paths.
[SDI-1] expected: The install and validation commands are part of the explicit apply/setup workflow, not hidden runtime behavior.
[SDI-2] expected: The shell commands are disclosed setup commands for installing, validating, showing diffs, and checking status; inspected scripts do not perform credential access or exfiltration.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad apply, routing, and memory trigger phrases are real reliability and consent considerations, but they are visible and serve the stated memory/context routing purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent memory writes are an intended feature of the memory commit workflow, though the workflow would be safer with a preview or explicit confirmation before writing.
